subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: Should STRICT migration preflight normalized collisions for secondary UNIQUE constraints, including documented handling for partial unique indexes, before this persisted-state repair lands?
rationale: The branch intentionally covers only primary keys while retaining a startup-blocking generic failure mode for a distinct class of persisted uniqueness constraints; choosing whether that is acceptable is an upgrade-policy decision, not a mechanical review judgment.

options.title: Cover all relevant UNIQUE constraints
options.body: Extend the migration to detect and report normalized collisions for secondary uniqueness constraints before copying rows, with focused tests for ordinary and partial-index behavior.

options.title: Accept the scoped primary-key-only policy
options.body: Land the narrower repair while explicitly accepting that affected secondary UNIQUE data can still require manual operator diagnosis after a generic migration failure.

options.title: Pause for migration-owner design
options.body: Hold this PR until the SQLite migration owner specifies a durable recovery contract for normalized secondary-UNIQUE collisions.

recommendation.title: Cover all relevant UNIQUE constraints
recommendation.body: Extend the migration to detect and report normalized collisions for secondary uniqueness constraints before copying rows, with focused tests for ordinary and partial-index behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged SQLite-safety change established the STRICT migration and its persisted-state safety contract.
